neutralityNote: priorityTopics selects WHICH stories to cover, never HOW to editorialize them. The wire-service voice (src/newswire/writing/prompts.ts) applies identically across every topic, including politics - 'liberal_democracy' and 'democratic_socialism' are coverage areas, not an instruction to inject opinion or bias.
topicGraphNote: Treat priorityTopics and watch as a connected graph, not a flat keyword whitelist: a story can qualify by being genuinely related to a node even if it doesn't literally name it. Example: a new Fontaines D.C. record is 'watch' (the band) -> 'music_genres_scenes' (post-punk) -> 'album_release_culture' (release/tour news) -> could also touch 'music_industry' (label deal, chart position). Follow those associative links when deciding what counts as on-topic, but every published claim still has to be independently verified - the graph only decides relevance, never overrides the verification/fact-check gates.
